description: cuSOLVER's per-matrix syevd serializes the dense batches (n=512 b640, n=1024 b60) and uses zero tensor cores. Build a genuinely BATCHED tensor-core eigensolver that fills the 148 SMs across the batch: blocked Householder tridiagonalization where panel trailing two-sided updates A-VW^T-WV^T are ONE batched FP16/BF16/TF32 tensor-core GEMM across ALL matrices at once (not per-matrix), compact-WY representation, FP32 reflector norms. Then a batched symmetric-tridiagonal solve (the existing bisection+twisted/Cuppen kernels), back-transform eigenvectors via one batched tensor-core GEMM through the WY reflectors. CholeskyQR2 FP32 Q-cleanup, L=diag(Q^T A Q). Route the dense n>=512 shapes here with residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback. The win is batch-concurrency saturating HBM, not a faster per-matrix algorithm.

TWO-STAGE tridiagonalization: dense->band (custom batched QR-panel kernel + batched GEMM two-sided update, tensor cores) + band->tridiag (latrd_panel) + GEMM back-transform. MULTI-CTA REDUCTION (coordinator's primary ask) - BUILT & BLOCKED:
- CUDA-GRAPHED cuBLAS reduction (matvec on the SHRINKING trailing block, multi-CTA, graph removes the ~2500 per-column launch overheads): measured 128ms (vs latrd 147ms), tridiag eig 1.3e-3, ZERO fallback. But INFEASIBLE -- harness validate.sh bans ANY 'stream' substring ('CUDA streams are banned by the leaderboard') and CUDA-graph capture requires torch.cuda.Stream. This kills the graph approach entirely on this leaderboard.
- COOPERATIVE-GRID (grid.sync between columns): cooperative launch needs ALL CTAs resident; measured cap = 1184 blocks at nt=256, so for b=640 only G=1 CTA/matrix fits (G=2 -> 1280 > 1184). Needs batch CHUNKING (C*G<=1184, e.g. C=148/G=8 over 5 chunks) -> a large fused kernel; left unbuilt because of the ceiling below.

THE DECISIVE CEILING (authoritative idle measurement, GPU exclusive):
- My best submittable pipeline (latrd) = 331ms on n512 b640 vs cuSOLVER 170ms (1.94x); 431ms vs 106ms on n1024 (4.05x).
- Component breakdown (n512 b640, idle): reduction(latrd) 147 + solve(incl 3ms bisect) 45 + WY back-transform 56 + final FP32 ortho 27 + 3-residual safety gate 56 = ~331ms.
- KEY: even with a FREE (0ms) reduction, the rest (solve 45 + backtransform 56 + ortho 27 + gate 56 = 184ms) ALREADY EXCEEDS cuSOLVER's 170ms total. So the multi-CTA reduction is NOT the binding constraint -- the back-transform + FP32 ortho + residual gate are. The coordinator's budget (backtransform+ortho=25ms) was ~6x optimistic; real = ~140ms. FP16/bf16 in back-transform/ortho broke orthogonality (>gate -> mass fallback), so they can't be cheapened that way.

CONCLUSION (measured, not assumed): the Householder-reduction mechanism is at best ~2x SLOWER than cuSOLVER on these dense shapes and cannot reach a geomean win under the leaderboard's constraints, because the eigenvector back-transform + FP32 orthonormalization + residual-gated-fallback verification (all O(n^3), all needed for FP32 correctness) sum above cuSOLVER's whole runtime independent of reduction speed.

BANKED ASSET worth carrying forward: the SMEM Sturm-bisection CUDA kernel (3ms vs cuSOLVER D&C; drop-in for tridiag_eigh) -- reusable by ANY brief that produces a tridiagonal d,e. It only pays off paired with a reduction+backtransform that are ALSO sub-cuSOLVER, which the GEMM-only spectral lines (brief 0 sign-split / brief 2 Chebyshev) achieve by SKIPPING tridiagonalization+back-transform entirely. RECOMMENDATION: the dense win lives on those lines, not the Householder mechanism; this brief's measured verdict is that Householder tridiagonalization is the wrong mechanism for THIS leaderboard's cost structure (solve+backtransform-dominated, FP32-output-gated). Remaining unbuilt-but-analyzed: the chunked cooperative reduction (ceiling = break-even at best, so low expected value); a band-aware two-stage stage-2 (would help the reduction but not the 184ms non-reduction floor).
